D1.seed_exact: bicycle automatic brake light — the inventor wants automatic brake indication without relying on manually pressing a light control

payloads.CTX: The decision is the braking-detection architecture. Candidate detection paths: (1) a wired brake-lever switch, (2) accelerometer-based inference of deceleration, (3) wheel-speed-based inference. On detected braking the brake light is driven on. Which detection path to adopt is exactly the unresolved decision.
payloads.REF: Components: a detection stage (one of the three candidates) and the indicator lamp it drives. Installation constraint: avoid or minimize a physical wire run to the brake lever, which weighs against candidate (1).
payloads.REASON: No calibration data or physical test results exist yet, and the acceptable false-positive rate under vibration is unspecified; those are missing evidence, not assumptions I can fill.

D3.seed_exact: a manually foldable wheelchair ramp for a home doorway — the inventor wants the ramp to stay reliably locked in the flat, load-bearing position and to fold away without tools

payloads.CTX: The decision is the folded-position retention architecture. Candidates: (1) over-centre toggle latch, (2) spring-loaded detent pin, (3) gravity-drop gate latch. The mechanism must retain the ramp in the flat, load-bearing position and release for tool-less folding.
payloads.REF: Force path: wheelchair load through the deployed ramp into the retention mechanism at the hinge line; manual actuation for fold and unfold; no permanent modification to the doorway or frame is permitted.
payloads.REASON: No load rating, retention margin, or physical test evidence exists; those are missing evidence, not assumptions I can fill.
